text:
henry: heads up — started seeing mid-SSE resets this morning. clients drop with '504 upstream reset' while auth rotation runs. pattern across eu-west/us-east and we see routes zigzag between pools. anyone else?

alina: yep, saw 3 incidents since 09:10. console shows route switch events at the same timestamps. 🙃

josh: logs look like proxy FIN immediately followed by 504 from upstream (<1s). hypothesis: sticky-lease gets invalidated during auth token refresh and client reconnects end up routed to a different pool. i can repro locally.

henry: can you paste the minimal repro (curl) + the request headers you used, and the console trace id if you have one?

josh: sure — here's the quick curl i used:
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token>' \  -H 'x-tenant: acct-42' \  -H 'x-resume-id: rsm-7b3f' \  'https://stream.redwood.example/v1/events'
```
and snippet from proxy logs: `proxy: connid=42 FIN -> proxied upstream 504, route=eu-west-1 -> us-east-2`

priya: if the client reconnects while routing flips, we end up double-counting streaming tokens — billing shows two active streams for the same resume id. console currently attributes usage per-route so customer sees double. we need server-side dedupe on resume id or a dedicated billing post-process to dedupe.

alina: we debated server-side dedupe before. concern is state explosion per-tenant if we keep resume ids. perhaps implement a small LRU with TTL and emit dedupe metrics so billing can be conservative.

henry: UX ask: console timeline should surface sticky-affinity changes and reasons (auth-rotate / capacity-shift / scale-down). right now the timeline only shows route assignment but not the trigger. can we add `route_affinity_change` events?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: stickyAffinityV2=false rolled to 10% at 2026-03-20T09:00Z (canary id: canary-891).

josh: ok — forcing clients off stickyAffinity during canary explains the zigzag. for dedupe i propose server accepts `x-resume-id` and dedupes within 2 minutes window. alternative: require signed `x-resume-hash` but that forces client KMS/signer changes.

priya: signed tokens are not realistic for web clients. we should not force client-side crypto. server-side LRU + TTL is fine, but we must keep eviction bounded per-tenant and emit `untrusted_resume` metric when resume id seen from new ip/route.

alina: compromise: accept plain `x-resume-id`, dedupe server-side in a small window, and add `resume.dedupe_hit` and `resume.untrusted` metrics. billing pipeline can suppress duplicates when `dedupe_hit>0` for the same resume in the window.

infra-bot: Created INF-3123: "SSE resume dedupe LRU + telemetry" and attached logs and repro. assigned to josh/priya. https://issues.redwood.example/INF-3123

henry: assigning console task too — CON-2045 to add `route_affinity_change` reason on timeline events. cc @consolebot.

consolebot: Created CON-2045 and added initial mockups (timeline row + reason dropdown). link: https://console.redwood.example/CON-2045

josh: i'll implement LRU dedupe (default 2m TTL, max 1000 keys per-tenant) and emit `resume.dedupe_hit`. will open a small PR and link to INF-3123.

henry: perfect. after deploy let's re-enable stickyAffinityV2 for canary and watch dedupe metrics. thanks all. :tada:
